title: New parking by-law and paid parking start
subtitle: Also: 2026 budget by-law, procedure by-law, community engagement strategy, tiered fire response, road salt referral.
overview: Council adopted a new Parking By-law and an Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) by-law {{vote:m10}}, moving parking enforcement from the provincial offences system to a township-run model. Paid parking is set to begin January 5, 2026. Council directed staff to raise the resident parking exemption to four registered vehicles per household after that date {{vote:m8}}, and added overnight winter parking exceptions for three downtown municipal lots {{vote:m9}}.

Council also approved the 2026 Budget by-law {{vote:m14}}, an interim tax levy {{vote:m13}} and a temporary borrowing by-law {{vote:m12}}. It passed an updated procedure by-law reflecting strong mayor powers {{vote:m5}}, and approved the Township's first Community Engagement Charter and Strategy {{vote:m6}}. The Fire Chief was authorized to sign a tiered response agreement with the paramedic service {{vote:m7}}.

Council referred a delegation's road salt pollution resolution to staff for a report {{vote:m3}}. The consent agenda, which included three heritage designation notices, was approved {{vote:m4}}. A closed session on the draft procedure by-law produced no report. The Mayor presented the Food Bank with a cheque from the Mayor's Golf Tournament.

decisions.detail: Council adopted a new Parking By-law and AMPS by-law, repealed the old parking and related by-laws, and included overnight parking exceptions for three municipal lots.
Staff were directed to change the exemption policy to allow four registered vehicles per household for Centre Wellington residents after January 5, 2026.
The parking by-law will exempt the lots at 160 Provost Lane, Menzies Lane and 25 Metcalfe from the November-to-March 2am-6am no-parking rule.
The Mayor and Clerk were authorized to execute the by-law formalizing adoption of the 2026 Budget.

decisions.item: Procedure by-law and strong mayor powers
decisions.detail: Council authorized a new procedure by-law governing Council and committee meetings, repealing By-law 2024-64.
Council approved the Township's first Community Engagement Charter and Strategy as outlined in Report CAO2025-24.
The salt pollution resolution from delegates was referred to staff for a report.
Authority was delegated to the Fire Chief to sign the tiered response letter of agreement with Guelph-Wellington Paramedic Service.

debate: On parking exemptions, several councillors said residents expected free parking and that a two-vehicle cap hurts multigenerational households and adult children. Staff said the cap kept manual approvals manageable, with about five staff processing roughly 100 applications a day, and that lifting it before January 5 would delay launch.

Staff also raised compliance concerns about having no cap, since plates are not cross-checked against the property address. Councillors proposed a limit of four per household after launch as a compromise. One councillor wanted a firm review date, while others preferred no deadline.

Councillors and staff discussed the three-hour limit and five-hour enforcement window in Zone 1. One councillor said residents may find it hard to understand. Staff said it is needed for turnover and enforcement, and that employees should use Zone 2.

Downtown residents had been ticketed for overnight parking in municipal lots, which led to the overnight exceptions. Councillors also asked about accessible spaces, unmarked residential streets, church parking and a possible mapping error on St. Patrick Street West.

On strong mayor powers, one councillor noted that a future mayor could regain hiring and dismissal authority the current Mayor has delegated back to staff. Delegates on road salt urged provincial liability reform and lower salt use; one councillor asked for time to read the resolution before any vote.
